newsitem.title: USA: Agriculture chief warns Floridians on strawberries.
newsitem.headline: Agriculture chief warns Floridians on strawberries.

text.p: Florida's Agriculture Commissioner told consumers Thursday to stay away from frozen strawberries packaged in California.
Responding to to an outbreak of Hepatitis A linked to Mexican-grown strawberries processed in California that have made at least 153 people ill, Commissioner of Agriculture Bob Crawford said:

"Right now, I, personally, would be very much on guard eating frozen strawberries labeled 'product of California.' Right now, personally, I would not eat any frozen strawberries that were the product of California."

The U.S. Centers for Disease Control said on Wednesday the only confirmed cases of people made sick by the nationally distributed berries were 153 schoolchildren and parents in Michigan. Tainted frozen strawberry desserts were distributed to schools in 28 Michigan counties as part of the federal school lunch program.
Although 3,000 cases were shipped to 24 school districts in Florida, the shipments were not part of the tainted lots that turned up in Michigan.
Crawford has ordered the product seized and urged federal officials Thursday to enact tougher labeling laws to tell consumers where produce was grown and processed.
In addition to institutional sales, Crawford said that an undisclosed amount of the frozen product was shipped to Florida retailers.
"I don't understand where the commissioner is getting his information," said Kevin Herglotz, spokesman for the California Department of Food and Agriculture.
"This only concerns bulk shipments that were processed during three days in 1996 and not shipped to retailers."
Hertglotz said there is no indication that retailers received any suspect product.
"If he's warning consumers to stay away for California frozen strawberries, he's scaring a heck of a lot of people for no reason," Hertglotz added.

Crawford also took a jab at Mexico, a frequent agricultural trading competitor for Florida, calling for federal labeling laws that would require country-of-origin information on fresh and processed food.
Florida is the only state to have state laws requiring the labeling of fresh fruit. Processed food is exempt.
"Our U.S. embassy says when you're in Mexico, don't eat fresh fruits and vegetables," Why should we be eating them here?"
